feature_contract.goal: Keep GOAL direct time/title glyph and queued sprite output under their exact producer through D3DX GPU batch submission, avoiding inherited previous-owner HUD double render.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Original 0xBE020 and 0xBE150 GOAL direct print helper edges, D3DX begin/draw/flush/end owner guard and regression; no global Flush, no result text B9200 changes, preserve +TIME, rank, time logic and unrelated world rendering.

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Both original GOAL direct helpers split a proven prior homogeneous source batch and submit remaining own homogeneous batches before semantic scope exits.
acceptance_items.behavior_area: Original GOAL source and D3DX GPU batching

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: Unknown, mixed, foreign, queued and failed D3DX batches keep original native End/error behavior.
acceptance_items.behavior_area: Foreign, mixed and queued D3DX fallback

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: R84 main DLL, R26 rollback, host, package and required exact-SHA gates succeed.
acceptance_items.behavior_area: R84 game, R26_SAFE rollback, host and packaging

trace_stages: Original 0xBE020/0xBE150 GOAL time/title helper calls produce immediate D3DX glyphs or enqueue separately tagged SpriteNodes with exact GOAL tokens.

The intercepted D3DXSprite Begin/Draw/Flush/End tracks the previously queued homogeneous producer, submits that prior GPU batch before a direct GOAL helper and submits a remaining exact GOAL batch before its source scope expires.

R84 physical D3D9 draw dispatch then classifies ScreenHud under the restored producer token for each actual GPU draw and composes separate per-eye OpenXR render targets through the existing host pipeline.
subcomponents: Producer lifetime: bracket both verified GOAL helper callsites with exact direct source ownership while preserving their separately tagged queued siblings and original return path.

GPU batch lifetime: split only tracked homogeneous preceding GOAL-boundary sprite work and submit any remaining GOAL-owned glyph triangles before changing exact semantic owner; fail closed for mixed/queued/foreign buffers.
Integrated R84 UI owner: retain the existing D3D9 source semantics through R33 stereo routing and x64 host while preserving R26_SAFE rollback, unrelated effects and protected input.

diagnosis.original_evidence: Source inspection at 224e6a9 exposed GOAL original print helper 0xBE020/0xBE150 entering ScopedExactProducerSemantic and immediately returning without a proven D3DXSprite deferred-batch GPU boundary; existing +TIME handled this independently and cannot automatically protect GOAL.
diagnosis.root_cause: Original GOAL helper's exact direct producer lifetime ended before a D3DXSprite Draw could be guaranteed submitted through Flush or End; an unrelated outgoing tracked batch also could be submitted under an incoming GOAL source. This is a source ownership defect; whether it caused the user's on-headset duplicated GOAL appearance is unproven.
source_trace: OutRun original BEA5A/BEA5F source E8 calls invoke GoalTime_TagHelper which dispatches the original 0xBE020/0xBE150 direct time/title glyph producer and separately records queued SpriteNode siblings.

Direct producer must flush a tracked homogeneous prior batch before taking ScreenHud GOAL token and submit any pending homogeneous own D3DX work before RAII restores the prior producer; queued work remains bound to SpriteNode producer at execution.

Actual D3D9 draw path R84 R33/ScreenHud then transmits each stereo eye through the existing x86-to-x64 OpenXR host; R26_SAFE remains explicit rollback and no generic WorldBillboard or SkyGlow policy is changed.
alternatives_rejected: Do not globally Flush each sprite or suppress pixels: ID3DXSprite batching is intentional and unrelated rank, SkyGlow, +TIME and alpha effects must remain separate.
Do not treat a passing static owner predicate or Windows CI as proof of Quest3 per-eye GOAL appearance; runtime remains UNTESTED.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: The exact GOAL token is carried until direct D3DX flush or stored on per-queued SpriteNodes, and stereo physical draw/host paths are untouched; Quest3 convergence remains untested.
